name: f-verb-high

content.text: Explain how a bicycle stays upright.

data.text:
A bicycle stays upright **while moving** because its direction of travel can change to keep its wheels underneath its center of mass.

If the bike starts to lean to one side, the rider—or the bike’s steering geometry—turns the front wheel slightly toward that side. The bike then curves beneath the leaning rider, bringing the wheels back under them. A rider does this constantly, often without noticing.

The bike’s geometry helps: the front wheel’s **trail** tends to make it steer in the direction the bike is leaning or drifting. The spinning wheels also have gyroscopic effects, which contribute, but they’re **not the main explanation**—bikes can be designed to balance without relying on them.

A bicycle isn’t inherently stable when it’s stopped. At very low speeds, steering corrections have little effect, so balancing becomes harder.
